chunks: And ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī, peace be upon him.
That he gave judgment concerning two men who disputed before him over a reed enclosure, and he said: “The reed enclosure belongs to the one on whose side the binding cords are attached.”

key_terms.الْقُمُطُ: the binding cords or ties fastened to the structure
key_terms.خُصٍّ: a reed enclosure or fence-like structure
key_terms.رَجُلَيْنِ: two men involved in the dispute

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام judge a property dispute over a reed enclosure?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal judgment from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding a dispute over a reed enclosure between two men. He determined ownership by the side to which its binding cords were attached, showing the use of physical indicators in judicial rulings.
